title: CORNER C5 Spec: The Platform
summary: C5 build spec. Self-service signup, XP/points UI, weekly recap animation, room editor, furniture marketplace, trend charts, ROI reports, skills marketplace, neighbor offices, push notifications, App Store listing. The stickiness layer.
content:
CORNER C5 Spec: The Platform

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 Depends on: C4 complete (Docker containers, provisioning API, WebSocket bridge, OTA updates, admin panel, data isolation) Unlocks: C6 (white-label, multi-language, voice interface, SDK, enterprise tier)

What C4 Delivered

C4 made Corner a real product. Docker container per client, <45s automated provisioning, WebSocket bridge over the internet, OTA skill updates, admin panel, 4-layer data isolation. Clients are paying. AOM manages 50 clients from one Hetzner server. Onboarding creates an account, spins up a container, and lands a client in their office with agents that know their business context.

C4 answered: "Can someone else use this?" Yes. And they pay for it.

C5 answers: "Why do they never leave?"

What C5 Is

C5 is the stickiness layer. Every feature increases switching cost, engagement frequency, and perceived value. If a client considers canceling after C5 ships, they're leaving behind: a customized world they built, accumulated XP and streaks, a furnished office they personalized, neighbor connections, a library of skills they depend on, months of ROI data proving the value.

C4 gets clients. C5 keeps them. The retention math: if C5 features push monthly churn from 5% to 2%, a 50-client base grows to 100 in 6 months instead of 14 months. Stickiness is the growth engine.

C5 North Star: After C5, a client who considers canceling feels the same way they'd feel about deleting their Instagram account. Too much invested. Too much to lose. Not because we trapped them, but because the world they built is genuinely theirs.

C5 Scope (Prioritized)

Tier 1: Must Ship (Revenue + Retention Core)

1. Self-Service Signup + Stripe Integration

C4 has human-gated onboarding. AOM reviews every submission before a container spins up. That works for 50 clients. It doesn't work for 500. C5 removes the gate.

C4 flow: Client completes onboarding > AOM reviews > Patrik/Ash approve > container spins up.

C5 flow: Client completes onboarding > card charged > container spins up instantly > AOM monitors via admin panel.

What changes:

  • Stripe integration. Subscription billing. Client selects plan during onboarding Step 6 (after "Describe your dream office," before room generation). Card tokenized via Stripe Elements. Subscription created on successful payment. Container provisioning triggered by Stripe checkout.session.completed webhook.
  • Free trial (7 days). Container spins up immediately on account creation. Full functionality, no feature gates. Credit card required at signup but not charged until day 8. Trial countdown visible in the HUD: "5 days left in your trial."
  • Auto-provisioning. No AOM approval. Container spins up within 2 minutes of completing onboarding. The provisioning API (from C4 Step 2) fires automatically on Stripe webhook, not on manual admin approval.
  • Cancellation flow. Client can cancel from Settings > Billing. Container stops at end of current billing period. Data archived to cold storage for 90 days. "We'll keep your office exactly as you left it for 90 days. Come back anytime." Cancellation survey (optional, 3 questions: why leaving, what would change your mind, would you recommend Corner).
  • Plan upgrades. Visible in the game: empty rooms where new agents could sit. Clicking an empty room shows "Add [Agent Type] - $X/month." Upgrade flow: select agent > confirm > Stripe updates subscription > container hot-updates with new agent > room populates with snap animation. Downgrade: agent walks to door, waves goodbye, room dims.
  • Failed payment handling. 3 retry attempts over 7 days. After 3 failures: container paused (not destroyed), client sees "Billing issue" banner with "Update Payment" button. 30 days grace before data archived.

Stripe webhook events to handle:

  • checkout.session.completed > trigger provisioning
  • invoice.paid > log payment, update admin panel
  • invoice.payment_failed > retry logic, notification to client + AOM admin
  • customer.subscription.updated > plan change, agent add/remove
  • customer.subscription.deleted > cancellation flow

Pricing plans in Stripe:

Plan Monthly Agents Features
Starter $1,500/mo 3 agents Core agents (Operations, Calendar, Email Triage)
Growth $3,000/mo 6 agents + Outreach, Content, Client Health
Scale $5,000/mo 10 agents + Full pipeline, custom agents, priority support
Enterprise Custom Unlimited Dedicated infrastructure, SLA, white-label (C6)

Conversion funnel math:

corner.app homepage
     |
     v (5% click "Get Started")
Account creation
     |
     v (80% complete onboarding)
Free trial starts (container live)
     |
     v (30% convert to paid after 7 days)
Paying client
     |
     v (95% monthly retention after C5 stickiness)
Long-term revenue

At 1,000 visitors/month:

  • 50 start onboarding
  • 40 complete and start trial
  • 12 convert to paid
  • $36k-60k new MRR per month (at $3-5k avg)

Combined with Jacob's outreach: target 5-10 clients/month manually while self-serve ramps.

Steffen design need: Pricing page. Plan comparison cards (3 tiers + enterprise CTA). Trial countdown HUD element. Cancellation flow (survey + "we'll keep your office" moment). Failed payment banner. Upgrade prompt on empty rooms (agent silhouette + "Add [Type]" CTA). Downgrade agent departure animation.

2. XP/Points System UI

C3 ships the XP data model (Supabase tables: xp_events, xp_totals). Data accumulates from C3 launch. By C5, there's months of agent activity ready to display. C5 renders it.

Party Screen level badges (Megaboard):

  • Agent level displayed as a badge on their Party Screen card
  • Level formula (from C3 data layer): level = floor(sqrt(total_xp / 100))
  • Visual: RPG-style level badge. Gold border, level number centered, progress bar to next level below
  • Animation: level-up triggers celebration in the agent's room (confetti burst, flash, optional fanfare sound)
  • Level displayed everywhere the agent appears: Party Screen, Checklist sidebar, room nameplate, chat header

Streak indicators:

  • Daily streak counter visible in the top-right HUD
  • Visual: flame icon with streak count
    • 3-day: small orange flame
    • 7-day: medium fire, slight pulse animation
    • 14-day: large fire with ember particles
    • 30-day: roaring blue flame, constant ambient glow
  • Streak multiplier shown: "2x" badge overlaid on the flame
  • Streak resets if no tasks completed in 24 hours (midnight to midnight, client timezone)
  • Streak warning push notification: "Your 14-day streak ends in 6 hours!" (ties into Push Notifications feature)

Progress bars:

  • XP progress bar below agent name in Party Screen (thin, subtle, gold fill)
  • Total business XP shown in HUD profile dropdown
  • Weekly XP earned shown in weekly recap
  • Level progress: "Level 5 -- 2,500 / 3,600 XP to Level 6"

Leaderboard (opt-in):

  • Anonymized by default. Clients can opt to show their company name in Settings > Profile > Leaderboard.
  • Rank by: total business XP (all-time) or weekly XP (this week). Toggle at top of leaderboard.
  • Visible at corner.app/leaderboard (public page) and in-app via Megaboard > Leaderboard tab.
  • Top 10 get a crown badge on their office exterior (visible to neighbors).
  • Privacy: participation is opt-in. Default is private. Toggling off removes you from the board instantly.
  • Refresh: leaderboard updates every hour (not real-time, prevents gaming).

XP balance (tuned for engagement):

Points need to feel achievable but meaningful. Not so easy everyone maxes in a week. Not so hard new users feel behind.

Action Base XP Notes
Task completed 10 Core engagement loop
Commit pushed 5 Rewards agent output
Handoff completed 3 Rewards pipeline flow
First message of the day 5 Daily login bonus
First task of the week 25 Monday motivation
Streak bonuses 1.5x-3x 3-day = 1.5x, 7-day = 2x, 14-day = 2.5x, 30-day = 3x
Milestone: 1st task 50 "Getting Started"
Milestone: 10th task 100 "Getting Serious"
Milestone: 100th task 500 "Operations Running"
Milestone: 1000th task 5,000 "AI-Powered Business"

Level milestones and unlocks:

Level XP Required Unlock
1 100 "Getting Started" badge
3 900 Choose 1 free furniture themed pack
5 2,500 Room color customization
10 10,000 "Office of the Month" nomination eligibility
20 40,000 Premium agent character skins
50 250,000 "Founding Member" permanent badge (early adopters only, expires after first 100 clients)

Steffen design need: Level badge design (gold border, number, multiple sizes for different contexts). Flame/streak icon (4 tiers with distinct visual escalation). XP progress bar style. Leaderboard layout (public page + in-app tab). Milestone achievement popup (centered modal with animation, auto-dismiss after 5s). Crown badge for top-10 (subtle, on building exterior). Agent character skins for Level 20 unlock (3-4 alternate color palettes per agent).

3. Weekly Recap Animation

Animated summary of what agents accomplished this week. Plays when client opens Corner on Monday morning (or on demand). This is the "is this worth it?" answer, delivered visually every single week.

What it shows (30-60 second animation):

  1. Title card. Fade in: "Week of March 10-16" in the Corner typeface. 2-second hold. Fade out.

  2. Agent highlights. For each agent with completions that week (sorted by task count, most productive first):

    • Camera pans to the agent's room (using the room zoom system from C3)
    • Agent character stands up, walks to center of room
    • Speech bubble: "[Agent Name] completed 5 tasks"
    • Quick scroll of task names in the bubble (1 second per 3 tasks, max 5 seconds)
    • Agent does a celebration animation (fist pump, nod, depends on personality)
    • Camera pans to next agent
    • Skip agents with 0 completions. Maximum 6 agents highlighted (prevents recap from being too long).

  3. Stats roll-up. Camera pulls back to full office view. Stats appear as floating overlays:

    • Total tasks completed: 23
    • Total messages exchanged: 147
    • Most active agent: Operations (8 tasks)
    • Streak status: "12-day streak, 2x multiplier active" (flame icon)
    • XP earned this week: 340
    • Business level: 5 (progress bar shows 65% to level 6)

  4. This week's priorities. Top 3 tasks from the upcoming task list appear as a to-do card overlay:

    • "1. Follow up with 3 leads"
    • "2. Publish weekly social content"
    • "3. Review Q1 financials"
    • Source: top 3 items from the Operations agent's task list, or manually pinned tasks

  5. Closing card. "Your team is ready. Let's go." 2-second hold. Fade to the live office.

Technical implementation:

  • Not pre-rendered video. Client-side animation using Framer Motion sequences. This keeps it lightweight (no server-side video generation) and allows real-time data.
  • Data source: Supabase query aggregating xp_events and tasks tables for the previous Monday-Sunday period.
  • Trigger: Auto-plays on first login between Monday 6:00 AM and Tuesday 6:00 AM (client timezone, stored in Supabase organizations.timezone).
  • "Seen" flag: recap_seen_week field in Supabase user_preferences. Set to current ISO week number after playback starts.
  • Watch Again: Button in the HUD dropdown menu: "Watch Weekly Recap." Available anytime.
  • Skip button: Top-right corner, appears after 3 seconds. Power users skip. That's fine.
  • Share: "Share Recap" button at the end. Generates a static image (screenshot of the stats roll-up) shareable via native share API or download. Not a video export (too heavy for C5).
  • Mobile: Same animation, responsive. Stats overlay uses mobile layout (stacked, not floating).

Steffen design need: Title card typography. Stats roll-up overlay layout (floating bubbles vs sidebar vs centered panel). Closing card design. "Share Recap" image template. Skip button placement and style. Agent celebration animation frames (2-3 frames per agent personality). Mobile stats layout.

Tier 2: Ship If Time (High-Value Stickiness)

4. Room Editor

Tap-to-place furniture. Customize your office. The Sims Mobile / Animal Crossing editor for your AI office.

Enter edit mode:

  • Game mode: "Edit" button appears when hovering over your room (desktop) or long-pressing (mobile)
  • Or: Settings > Rooms > [Room Name] > Edit Layout
  • Edit mode only available for rooms in your org (can't edit neighbor offices)

Editor UI:

  • Room fills the viewport (zoom Level 3 from C3)
  • Left sidebar: furniture inventory. All owned furniture items as sprite thumbnails. Grouped by category (desks, chairs, decor, tech, plants). Search/filter bar at top.
  • Grid overlay on the room floor. Isometric grid snapping. Grid cells match the grid_size from the furniture data model.
  • Drag: furniture from sidebar to room. Ghost preview shows valid/invalid placement (green tint = valid, red tint = collision or out of bounds).
  • Rotate: click placed item > rotate button (or R key). 4 orientations (0, 90, 180, 270).
  • Delete: drag item back to sidebar, or select item > Delete key / trash icon.
  • Save: "Save" button (top-right). Writes furniture config to Supabase room_furniture table. Success toast: "Room saved."
  • Cancel: "Cancel" button. Reverts to pre-edit state. Confirmation if changes exist: "Discard changes?"
  • Undo/Redo: Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z. History stack of up to 20 actions.

Placement rules:

  • Desk + chair are mandatory per room. Cannot be removed, only swapped for different desk/chair items.
  • Monitor must be on a desk surface (checks adjacency, not just grid position).
  • Maximum furniture items per room: 10. Prevents visual clutter. Counter shown: "7/10 items."
  • Collision detection: items can't overlap. Grid-based, not pixel-based.
  • Wall-mounted items (posters, clocks, shelves): snap to wall segments only. Different placement grid (vertical vs floor).
  • Floor items can't overlap wall-mounted items (different z-layers, but same grid footprint check not needed).

Technical:

  • Furniture config stored per room in Supabase room_furniture table (same schema as C3's swappable JSON config):
    {
  "room_id": "bobby",
  "org_id": "uuid",
  "furniture": [
    {
      "item_id": "standing-desk-modern",
      "grid_position": [2, 1],
      "rotation": 0,
      "z_index": 10
    }
  ],
  "updated_at": "2026-03-16T14:30:00Z"
}
  • Editor is a React component layered on top of the existing room renderer from C3
  • Drag-and-drop via @dnd-kit/core (same library as Checklist mode, shared dependency)
  • Grid snapping: round drop coordinates to nearest valid grid position
  • Collision check: compare grid_position + grid_size of all placed items. Reject if overlap.
  • Changes sync to the container: visual config in Supabase, container reads on boot. Room re-renders in real-time for all connected clients in the same org (via Supabase real-time subscription on room_furniture table).
  • Optimistic updates: room re-renders immediately on save, Supabase write is async.

Steffen design need: Edit mode UI (sidebar, grid overlay, hover states). Furniture inventory sidebar layout. Ghost preview for drag (valid/invalid tinting). Rotate/delete controls on selected item. Save/cancel toolbar. "7/10 items" counter style. Wall-mounted placement indicator. Mobile editor layout (bottom sheet inventory instead of sidebar).

5. Furniture Marketplace

Starter furniture is free with every room. Themed packs available for purchase. The Fortnite model: free to play (the game view is always there), pay for cosmetics (furniture personalizes the experience).

Furniture data model (extends C3's JSON config):

{
  "id": "standing-desk-modern",
  "name": "Standing Desk (Modern)",
  "pack_id": "tech-startup",
  "sprite": "/sprites/furniture/standing-desk-modern.png",
  "sprite_rotations": [
    "/sprites/furniture/standing-desk-modern-0.png",
    "/sprites/furniture/standing-desk-modern-90.png",
    "/sprites/furniture/standing-desk-modern-180.png",
    "/sprites/furniture/standing-desk-modern-270.png"
  ],
  "grid_size": [2, 1],
  "placement": "floor",
  "price_type": "pack",
  "unlock_condition": null,
  "tags": ["desk", "modern", "tech"],
  "created_at": "2026-03-16"
}

Packs to design (Steffen's domain):

Pack Theme Items Price Notes
Starter Default desk, chair, monitor, lamp, plant Free Included with every room
Tech Startup Silicon Valley standing desk, VR headset, whiteboard, RGB keyboard, lava lamp $29 Most popular predicted

Revenue model:

  • Starter pack: free (included with every room, cannot be purchased separately)
  • Themed packs: $19-39 one-time purchase per pack
  • Individual premium items: $5-15 each (unlocked for purchase only after buying at least one pack)
  • Earned items: unlocked via XP milestones (Level 3 = free themed pack choice, Level 5 = room color, Level 20 = skins)
  • Brand partnerships (C6+): real brands (Herman Miller, IKEA) pay AOM for placement. Their products in the game. Kept for C6 because it requires business development.

Purchase flow:

  1. Client opens Room Editor (or Settings > Furniture Store)
  2. "Store" tab in sidebar shows all available packs and items
  3. Client clicks a pack > preview modal shows all 5 items in context (isometric room render with the pack's items placed)
  4. "Buy for $29" button > Stripe Checkout (one-time payment, not subscription)
  5. Stripe webhook checkout.session.completed > add pack items to client_furniture_inventory table
  6. Items immediately appear in the editor sidebar under "Owned"
  7. Toast: "Tech Startup pack unlocked! Start decorating."

Supabase tables:

  • furniture_catalog: all available items (id, name, pack_id, sprite, grid_size, placement, price_type, tags)
  • furniture_packs: pack definitions (id, name, description, price_cents, stripe_price_id, preview_image, seasonal_start, seasonal_end)
  • client_furniture_inventory: owned items per org (org_id, item_id, source: "purchase" | "earned" | "starter", acquired_at)
  • room_furniture: placed items per room (from Room Editor spec above)

Steffen design need: 5-item sprite sheets for each pack (4 rotations per item = 20 sprites per pack). Pack preview images (isometric room with all 5 items placed, marketing quality). Store UI layout (pack cards with preview, price, "Buy" CTA). Individual item cards. "Owned" vs "Not Owned" visual distinction in editor sidebar. Seasonal pack badge ("Limited Time" ribbon). Earned item badge ("Unlocked" with level icon).

6. Trend Charts + ROI Reports

Per-client analytics dashboard in the Megaboard. The "is this worth it?" answer backed by data, delivered automatically.

Charts (Megaboard > Analytics tab):

  • Tasks completed per week (line chart, 12-week trailing). X-axis: weeks. Y-axis: task count. Tooltip: "Week of Mar 10: 23 tasks." Color: Corner brand primary.
  • Response time trend (line chart, 12-week trailing). Average time from client message to first agent token. Trend line showing if it's getting faster. Target: <2s.
  • Agent utilization heatmap (grid chart). X-axis: days of week. Y-axis: agents. Cell color intensity = task count. "Bobby is busiest on Tuesdays."
  • Messages per day (bar chart, last 30 days). Simple daily message volume. Shows engagement patterns.
  • XP growth curve (line chart, all-time). Cumulative XP over time. Shows acceleration from streak multipliers.
  • Streak history (calendar heatmap, GitHub contribution graph style). Each day colored by activity level. Current streak highlighted.

Chart library: Recharts (React, declarative, responsive, already common in Next.js). Alternatively, Tremor (built for dashboards, simpler API). Bobby's call.

ROI Report (monthly, auto-generated):

Generated on the 1st of each month for the previous month. Available in Megaboard > Reports tab and delivered via email.

Report contents:

  • "Your AI team handled 47 tasks this month" (from tasks table, status = done, date range filter)
  • "Estimated hours saved: 23.5 hours" (benchmark: 30 minutes per task average. Configurable per agent type in agent_benchmarks table.)
  • "At $75/hour, that's $1,762 in value delivered" (hourly rate set during onboarding or in Settings > Company Profile)
  • "Your Corner subscription: $3,000/month"
  • "Net ROI: -$1,238" or "+$2,762" (value delivered minus subscription)
  • Comparison to previous month: "+12 tasks (+34%), +6 hours saved"
  • Agent breakdown: which agents delivered the most value
  • Top tasks completed (5 most impactful)
  • Trend spark-line (last 6 months of ROI)

Why ROI matters: If the ROI number is > 3x the monthly fee, the client never questions the subscription. That's the retention target. If ROI is negative, the admin panel flags this client as churn risk and AOM proactively reaches out.

PDF export: "Download Report" button generates a branded PDF (Corner logo, client company name, month/year). Uses @react-pdf/renderer or server-side generation via Puppeteer on the admin server.

Email delivery: Monthly ROI email to the org owner. Subject: "Your Corner ROI Report: March 2026." Body: key stats with "View Full Report" CTA linking to the in-app report. Sent via Resend or Postmark (transactional email, not marketing).

Admin panel view: AOM admin sees ROI reports for all clients. Sorted by ROI (lowest first = highest churn risk). Red flag on clients with negative ROI for 2+ consecutive months.

Steffen design need: Chart styling (colors, typography, axis labels, tooltips consistent with Corner brand). ROI report layout (in-app and PDF). "Download Report" button placement. Email template design. Admin panel ROI overview (client ROI grid with color coding). Streak calendar heatmap cell design.

Tier 3: Platform Differentiation

7. Skills Marketplace

Skills are the "apps" of the Corner platform. AOM builds them, clients use them. C5 builds the gallery and distribution. C6 opens it to third-party developers.

Free Core Skills (GitHub: mrg33k/corner-skills, public repo):

Open source. Anyone can use these in any Claude Code setup, not just Corner. Marketing tool.

  • Calendar management
  • Email triage
  • Task management
  • Meeting notes summarizer
  • Invoice reminders
  • Social media scheduling (basic)
  • Client follow-up system

Each skill: SKILL.md + supporting files. README links to Corner for the full experience. "These skills work anywhere. They work best in Corner."

Premium Skills (Corner platform only):

Available to Corner platform subscribers. These differentiate the paid product. Cannot be extracted from the container (obfuscated, integrity-checked by the Skill Sync Agent from C4).

  • Full multi-agent orchestration (Mom skill)
  • Industry-specific agent packs:
    • CPA Pack: tax deadline tracker, client document collector, IRS update monitor
    • Contractor Pack: bid estimator, permit tracker, subcontractor scheduler
    • Law Firm Pack: case timeline, billing hours tracker, precedent research
    • Healthcare Pack: appointment scheduler, insurance verification, patient follow-up
  • Advanced QA pipeline (Elmo skill)
  • Client health scoring (Paige skill)
  • Competitive intelligence (Alex skill)
  • Automated outreach (Jacob skill)
  • Content production pipeline (Cleo skill)
  • Brand enforcement (Steffen skill)

Premium skill pricing:

  • Included with Growth and Scale plans (bundled, not itemized)
  • Starter plan: 3 premium skills included, additional at $99/month each
  • Industry packs: $199/month add-on (or included with Scale plan)

Skills Gallery UI:

On corner.app (public page: corner.app/skills):

  • Browse skills by category (Productivity, Communication, Sales, Finance, Operations, Industry-Specific)
  • Skill card: icon, name, one-line description, "Free" or "Premium" badge, install count, star rating
  • Skill detail page: full description, screenshots/demo video, requirements, changelog, "Install" CTA
  • "Install" button behavior: if not logged in > "Sign up for Corner." If logged in + free skill > installs to container. If logged in + premium > shows plan requirement or purchase flow.

In-app (Settings > Skills):

  • Installed skills list with version, last update date, enable/disable toggle
  • "Browse Skills" opens gallery in-app (same UI, no context switch)
  • Auto-update toggle per skill (default: on)
  • Skill health indicator: green (working), yellow (needs update), red (broken/disabled)
  • "Request a Skill" form (client describes what they want, routes to AOM for custom development)

Skill package format:

skill-name/
  SKILL.md            # Skill definition (triggers, instructions, outputs)
  README.md           # Gallery description, screenshots
  skill-meta.json     # Version, dependencies, pricing tier, category
  supporting-files/   # Templates, prompts, data files

skill-meta.json:

{
  "name": "invoice-reminders",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "author": "AOM",
  "tier": "free",
  "category": "Finance",
  "description": "Automatically sends invoice reminders based on aging thresholds.",
  "dependencies": [],
  "min_corner_version": "C5",
  "icon": "invoice-icon.png"
}

Steffen design need: Skills gallery page layout (grid of skill cards). Skill card design (icon, name, description, badges). Skill detail page layout. In-app skills settings panel. "Free" vs "Premium" badge styles. Industry pack banner images. "Request a Skill" form.

8. Neighbor Offices / Social Layer

Your Corner has neighbors. Other Corner users (opt-in). See their office exterior from your isometric view. Click to visit (read-only). Social proof drives upgrades. Community builds retention.

Visibility tiers (client controls, Settings > Privacy):

  • Private (default): nobody can see your office. You have no neighbors.
  • Building Only: your office exterior visible to matched neighbors. Interior hidden. They see the building, room count, and business level badge.
  • Open Office: neighbors can peek inside (see room layout, furniture, agent names). Not actual data, tasks, or conversations.
  • Public: anyone on corner.app can visit your office (marketing/showcase). AOM features these on the homepage.

Neighbor matching algorithm:

  • Automatic: matched with 4-6 offices. Criteria: same plan tier, similar industry (from onboarding), similar activity level (XP within 2 levels), same geographic region (from onboarding).
  • Manual: invite specific companies by email. "Add Neighbor" in Settings > Neighbors. Recipient accepts/declines.
  • AOM curated: AOM features active/interesting offices as "featured neighbors." Visible to everyone on Building Only+ visibility. Rotating weekly.

Visit experience (Game mode):

  • Click neighbor building from your isometric view (they appear as smaller buildings adjacent to your office, outside your building's walls)
  • Camera pans to their office (smooth transition, 500ms)
  • See their room layout, furniture, agent names and types (not tasks/data)
  • See their business level badge
  • Guest book: leave a one-line message (max 100 chars). "Nice setup!" or "Love the zen garden." Guest book visible in Settings > Neighbors > Messages.
  • "Inspired?" CTA button: returns to your own office, opens room editor. Conversion tool.
  • "Back to My Office" button in top-left.
  • Visit duration: no limit. But no real-time data visible, so it's a quick browse.

Social features (light touch, not a social network):

  • Neighbor count badge on your office exterior (small number)
  • "Office of the Month" feature on corner.app homepage. Nominated by reaching Level 10+. Voted by neighbors (1 vote per account per month). Winner gets a trophy furniture item.
  • Achievement sharing (opt-in): "Phoenix CPA Group hit Level 10!" notification to neighbors.
  • Seasonal events: "Holiday decoration contest." Most festive office (neighbor votes) wins a limited-edition furniture pack.

Privacy rules (HARD, NON-NEGOTIABLE):

  • NO business data exposed to visitors. Zero.
  • NO task lists, conversation history, agent outputs, messages, files, or reports visible.
  • NO analytics or metrics visible to visitors (not even aggregated).
  • Only visible: room layout, furniture, agent names/types, business level, guest book.
  • Client controls every layer of visibility. One toggle to go fully private, takes effect immediately.
  • AOM never shares client list externally without explicit written consent.
  • Neighbor matching data (industry, region) never exposed to other clients.
  • Guest book messages are moderated (simple profanity filter + report button).

Steffen design need: Neighbor building exterior sprites (small isometric building, shows room count, level badge, neighbor count). Visit mode UI (read-only indicator, guest book input, "Back to My Office" button, "Inspired?" CTA). Office of the Month trophy item. Seasonal event badges. Neighbor list in Settings (avatar/company name, level, last active).

Tier 4: Re-engagement + Distribution

9. Push Notifications (Enhanced)

C3 PWA supports basic notifications. C5 makes them strategic re-engagement tools.

Notification types:

Type Trigger Message When
Task completed task_complete event "[Agent] completed: [task name]" Real-time
Agent blocked Agent error + no recovery in 60s "[Agent] needs your input" Real-time
Daily summary Cron (8 AM client timezone) "Your team completed 7 tasks yesterday" Daily
Streak warning Streak > 7 days + no activity by 6 PM "Your 14-day streak ends in 6 hours!" Conditional
Weekly recap ready Monday 6 AM "Your weekly recap is ready. See what your team accomplished." Weekly
ROI report ready 1st of month "Your March ROI report is in." Monthly
Trial ending Day 5 of trial "Your free trial ends in 2 days. Keep your office running." Once
New skill available OTA skill push "New skill: Invoice Reminders. Install now." On push
Neighbor activity Neighbor levels up (opt-in) "Phoenix CPA Group just hit Level 10!" Event
Furniture sale Seasonal pack drops "Summer Pack is here. Limited time." Seasonal

Implementation:

  • Web Push API (service worker, push subscription stored in Supabase push_subscriptions)
  • Push server: lightweight Node.js service on the admin server (web-push npm library)
  • Notification preferences in Settings > Notifications (per-type toggle, quiet hours setting)
  • Quiet hours default: 9 PM - 7 AM client timezone. Notifications queue and deliver at 7 AM.
  • Badge count: PWA badge API for unread task completions (shows on app icon)

Steffen design need: Notification preference panel layout (toggles per type, quiet hours picker). Push notification visual on iOS/Android (icon, title, body preview). Badge icon for PWA.

10. App Store Listing

PWA can be submitted to Apple App Store and Google Play Store. This is marketing and distribution, not a separate build. Same PWA, just listed in stores.

Apple App Store (via PWA):

  • Submit using Safari's "Add to Home Screen" deeplink + App Store listing via PWABuilder
  • Alternatively: thin Capacitor wrapper (same PWA, native shell for store listing)
  • App name: "Corner: AI Office"
  • Category: Productivity > Business
  • Screenshots: Game view, Checklist, Megaboard, mobile chat, weekly recap
  • App Store review considerations: must demonstrate real functionality (not just a web wrapper). The PWA's offline mode, push notifications, and native-feel interactions should satisfy this.

Google Play Store (via TWA):

  • Trusted Web Activity (TWA) via Bubblewrap. No code changes. Just packaging.
  • Same screenshots and metadata as Apple.

Desktop app (lower priority):

  • If demand exists: Tauri wrapper (Rust, lightweight, <10MB binary)
  • Menu bar icon showing active agent count and status
  • System notifications for task completions
  • Only build if >20% of users request desktop app. PWA should handle most desktop use cases.

Steffen design need: App Store screenshots (5-6 screens, device frames, feature callouts). App icon (Corner logo, iOS/Android guidelines). Feature graphic for Google Play (1024x500). App Store description copy.

What C5 Unlocks

  1. Self-service revenue. Clients sign up and pay without AOM touching anything. Revenue scales with traffic, not with AOM's time.

  2. 95%+ retention. XP, streaks, furniture, neighbors, and weekly recaps create switching cost that goes beyond the product's utility. Clients stay because their world is theirs.

  3. Cosmetic revenue stream. Furniture packs generate revenue with zero marginal cost. $29 per pack, unlimited inventory. If 30% of 50 clients buy 2 packs: $870 incremental revenue per cohort.

  4. Data-backed retention conversations. When a client considers canceling, AOM can show: "Your team saved you 47 hours last month. At your rate, that's $3,525 in value for your $3,000 subscription." Numbers end cancellation conversations.

  5. Platform stickiness moat. Competitors can copy the AI backend. They can't copy the world a client built: their furniture, their level, their streak, their neighbors. That's personal, not technical.

  6. App Store presence. Corner listed in Apple App Store and Google Play. Discoverability. Credibility. "Download Corner" in sales materials.

  7. Skills as a distribution channel. Free skills on GitHub drive awareness. "Built for Corner" badge on free skills funnels developers and businesses to the paid product.

  8. C6 readiness. White-label needs the furniture marketplace, skills gallery, and self-service signup to exist. Enterprise tier needs trend charts and ROI reports. Voice interface needs the established chat and agent architecture. C5 is the foundation for everything C6 adds.

What C5 Does NOT Include

Explicitly out of scope for C5. These are C6+ features:

  • White-label Corner. Agencies/consultants resell Corner under their own brand. C6.
  • Third-party skill development. Developer portal, skill submission, review process, revenue share. C6.
  • Multi-language support. Corner in Spanish, Japanese, German. C6.
  • Voice interface. Talk to agents via voice. C6.
  • Video agents. Agents that see via camera, produce video. C6.
  • API marketplace. Third-party integrations (QuickBooks, Salesforce). C6.
  • Enterprise tier features. SSO, SLA, dedicated infrastructure. C6.
  • Corner SDK. Developers build apps on top of Corner. C6.
  • AI-to-AI marketplace. Cross-client agent collaboration. C6.
  • Brand partnerships for furniture. Real brand products (Herman Miller, IKEA) in the marketplace. C6+.
  • Custom furniture commissions. Client describes, Steffen/Gemini generates. C6+.
  • Room bonuses from furniture. Mechanical effects (e.g., "better desk = agent works faster"). C6+ gimmick, purely cosmetic in C5.
  • Desktop app (Tauri). Only if >20% demand after PWA + App Store.
  • Multi-region deployment. US East handles C5 scale.

Supabase Schema Additions (C5)

-- Subscriptions
CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id UUID REFERENCES organizations(id),
  stripe_customer_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  stripe_subscription_id TEXT,
  plan TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (plan IN ('starter', 'growth', 'scale', 'enterprise')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('trialing', 'active', 'past_due', 'canceled', 'paused')),
  trial_end TIMESTAMPTZ,
  current_period_end TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Furniture catalog
CREATE TABLE furniture_catalog (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  pack_id TEXT REFERENCES furniture_packs(id),
  sprite TEXT NOT NULL,
  sprite_rotations JSONB DEFAULT '[]',
  grid_size INTEGER[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{1,1}',
  placement TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (placement IN ('floor', 'wall', 'desk')),
  price_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (price_type IN ('free', 'pack', 'premium', 'earned')),
  unlock_condition JSONB,
  tags TEXT[] DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Furniture packs
CREATE TABLE furniture_packs (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  stripe_price_id TEXT,
  preview_image TEXT,
  seasonal_start DATE,
  seasonal_end DATE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Client owned furniture
CREATE TABLE client_furniture_inventory (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id UUID REFERENCES organizations(id),
  item_id TEXT REFERENCES furniture_catalog(id),
  source TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('starter', 'purchase', 'earned', 'gift')),
  acquired_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(org_id, item_id)
);

-- Room furniture placements
CREATE TABLE room_furniture (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  room_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  org_id UUID REFERENCES organizations(id),
  furniture JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(room_id, org_id)
);

-- Push notification subscriptions
CREATE TABLE push_subscriptions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id),
  endpoint TEXT NOT NULL,
  keys JSONB NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Notification preferences
CREATE TABLE notification_preferences (
  user_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.users(id),
  task_complete BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  agent_blocked BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  daily_summary BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  streak_warning BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  weekly_recap BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  roi_report BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  trial_ending BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  new_skill BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  neighbor_activity BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
  furniture_sale BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  quiet_hours_start TIME DEFAULT '21:00',
  quiet_hours_end TIME DEFAULT '07:00'
);

-- Guest book entries (neighbor visits)
CREATE TABLE guest_book_entries (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  host_org_id UUID REFERENCES organizations(id),
  visitor_org_id UUID REFERENCES organizations(id),
  message TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(message) <= 100),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Neighbor relationships
CREATE TABLE neighbor_connections (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_a UUID REFERENCES organizations(id),
  org_b UUID REFERENCES organizations(id),
  source TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('auto', 'manual', 'curated')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('active', 'pending', 'declined')),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(org_a, org_b)
);

-- Leaderboard (materialized view, refreshed hourly)
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW leaderboard AS
SELECT
  o.id AS org_id,
  o.name AS org_name,
  o.leaderboard_visible,
  xt.total_xp,
  xt.level,
  xt.streak_days,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY xt.total_xp DESC) AS rank_all_time,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY weekly.xp DESC) AS rank_weekly
FROM organizations o
JOIN xp_totals xt ON xt.org_id = o.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT org_id, SUM(points) AS xp
  FROM xp_events
  WHERE created_at > now() - INTERVAL '7 days'
  GROUP BY org_id
) weekly ON weekly.org_id = o.id
WHERE o.leaderboard_visible = true;

-- ROI reports
CREATE TABLE roi_reports (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id UUID REFERENCES organizations(id),
  month DATE NOT NULL,
  tasks_completed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  estimated_hours_saved NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  hourly_rate NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 75,
  value_delivered NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  subscription_cost NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  net_roi NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  report_data JSONB,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(org_id, month)
);

-- RLS policies (all tables scoped to org_id via auth.jwt() -> org_id claim)
-- Follow C4's RLS pattern: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE where org_id = auth.jwt()->>'org_id'

Push Notification Server

  • Runs on the admin server alongside the provisioning API and updater
  • web-push npm library for VAPID-based push
  • VAPID keys generated once, stored in environment variables
  • Cron jobs (node-cron):
    • Daily summary: 8 AM per client timezone
    • Streak warning: 6 PM per client timezone (check streak > 7, no activity today)
    • Weekly recap: Monday 6 AM per client timezone
    • ROI report: 1st of month per client timezone
  • Event-driven notifications (task_complete, agent_blocked, new_skill): triggered by WebSocket events from containers, routed through admin server

Transactional Email

  • Service: Resend or Postmark (both have generous free tiers, reliable delivery)
  • Templates:
    • Monthly ROI report email
    • Trial ending reminder
    • Failed payment notice
    • Neighbor invite
    • Office of the Month winner announcement
  • From address: team@corner.app (or team@aheadofmarket.com until Corner domain purchased)
  • Unsubscribe: managed via notification preferences (link in every email)

Chart Library

Bobby's choice between:

  • Recharts: Most popular React chart library. Declarative API. Good defaults. SSR-friendly.
  • Tremor: Purpose-built for dashboards. Simpler API. Fewer customization options.
  • Nivo: More visual chart types (heatmaps, calendars). Heavier bundle.

Recommendation: Recharts for standard charts (line, bar) + Nivo for heatmap/calendar views. Or Tremor if Bobby wants simplicity.

C6 Horizon (Early Thinking)

What comes after C5? Not spec'd yet. These are captured ideas for the next cycle.

  • White-label Corner. Agencies/consultants resell Corner under their own brand. AOM powers the backend.
  • Multi-language support. Corner in Spanish, Japanese, German. Expands TAM globally.
  • Voice interface. Talk to agents via voice (ElevenLabs or Whisper). Walk into your isometric office, speak, agents respond.
  • Corner SDK. Developers build entire apps on top of the Corner platform.
  • Enterprise tier. SSO, SLA, dedicated infrastructure, audit logs, custom SLAs.
  • Third-party skill marketplace. Developer portal, skill submission, review, 70/30 revenue share.
  • AI-to-AI marketplace. Agents from different clients collaborate (permission-gated).
  • Brand furniture partnerships. Real brands pay for placement.
  • API marketplace. QuickBooks, Salesforce, HubSpot as one-click installs.

C5 is where Corner stops being a tool and becomes a world people live in. Every feature increases the cost of leaving and the joy of staying. That's the formula: utility (C1-C4) times delight (C5) equals retention.

"A million worlds, and yours keeps getting better."
